technical_and_design_decisions: Baseline toolchain is Java 17+ with Spring Framework 6.x / Spring Boot 3.x, Maven/Gradle build, per the specification preamble.
Unit tests are implemented with JUnit 5, Mockito, and Spring Test; integration tests use Spring Boot test slices plus embedded or containerized infrastructure (e.g., Testcontainers) where feasible.
YARN SPI integration tests run against a Hadoop MiniYARNCluster-based test fixture or an existing dedicated test YARN cluster, triggered by a dedicated CI profile.
Cloud Foundry (CC) SPI integration tests run against an available CF test foundation; where no foundation is reachable, CF client interactions are covered with recorded/mocked stubs in CI.
Integration tests for all SPIs are wired into the existing CI pipeline as separate jobs/profiles so failures are isolated and do not block unit-test stages.

U7 fix targets the container lifecycle/shutdown path in the deployer/Admin layer: graceful stop of the JDBC source poller and HDFS sink, bounded executor shutdown with timeout, and cleanup of deployment state so Admin UI shutdown completes.

U8 is implemented by extending the binder configuration model (e.g., spring.cloud.stream.binders.* entries with per-binder environment/connection-factory settings) so bindings can reference a named binder; full backward compatibility with a single default binder is preserved.
Documentation (U1 and U8 docs) is written in Asciidoc and added to the existing reference documentation module.
Code review feedback is incorporated within each implementation activity rather than as separate activities.
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates are effort (workdays), not elapsed duration.
The {{Lattice}}, {{CC}}, {{YARN}}, and {{container}} placeholders refer to existing, buildable deployer SPI modules in the current codebase.
Existing build system, source control, and CI infrastructure are available and functional; no pipeline platform needs to be created from scratch.

Test infrastructure (YARN test cluster or MiniYARNCluster dependencies, a CF test foundation or stubs, and an Oracle-compatible database for reproducing U7) is available or can be provisioned with containers without separate procurement effort.
The U7 shutdown defect reproduces in the target environment and its root cause lies within project code, not in third-party libraries.
No large-scale refactoring is required beyond the scope described in the user stories.
Existing test suites are green at the start of the increment; effort for fixing unrelated pre-existing failures is excluded.
Documentation publishing uses the existing docs build/publish process.
